newsitem.title: BRAZIL: FORECAST - Brazil Nov trade gap seen at $900 mln.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Brazil Nov trade gap seen at $900 mln.

text.p: Brazil is expected to post a trade deficit of around $900 million in November as import levels are seen returning to more traditional levels after setting a worrying record high in October.

Analysts said the lower trade gap should reflect a drop in fuel, consumer and capital good imports, which rose sharply in the two preceding months as manufacturers boosted output levels previous to the Christmas and yearend sales sales.
"We should see imports falling back in November," said Jose Antonio Pena, senior economist at Banco de Boston.
Pena said there were also signs fuel imports, which rose to unusually high levels of $665 million in September and $680 million in October, should not exceed $450 million in November.

October's whopping $1.308 billion trade gap forced virtually all Brazil-watchers to reconsider their trade projections for the year and has raised questions about the sustainability of the foreign exchange policy currently in place.
Brazil October imports totalled $5.496 billion while exports were $4.188 billion.

"Most of us expect the November trade data will show a return to better-known territory. If they don't, then we'll really begin to worry about the country's external accounts," said an economist at a major Brazilian investment bank.

A recent Reuters consensus survey of eight Brazilian brokerages and research firms saw a November deficit of $919 million. However it is worth noting the researchers' forecasts cover a relatively wide range from a low of $692 million to a high of $1.040 billion.
The consensus forecast from the same research houses put the final 1996 trade deficit at $4.7 billion.
On December 3 Brazil reported November exports totalled $3.912 billion, down from $4.188 billion in October.
